name: von_karman_viscous_pump
title: von Karman's viscous pump (rotating disk)
summary: Solution of the von Karman viscous pump problem (White, Viscous Fluid Flow, 2005, p. 162): three coupled differential equations in the similarity variables f, g and h are integrated with the Integral function from x = 0 to x = 10, the two slopes at the origin being determined by a shooting method.
language_features: prime notation in the variable names (not supported by CoolSolve)

verification.summary: Runnable variant vs the EES stored solution of the binary source: 11 common variables, 1 differ (rtol=0.001); the stored Obj is stale (it does not equal |g|+|f| of the stored f and g) and is excluded. The shooting slopes agree with White (2005, p. 162) to 5.2e-05 and 4.1e-05 relatively.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/EES_library/von Karman.EES (11 decoded variables); shooting solution of the model (f'(0) = 0.510213591117, g'(0) = -0.615909650561) against the published values of White, Viscous Fluid Flow, (2005) p. 162 (f'(0) = 0.5102, g'(0) = -0.6159)
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 11 common variables, 1 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 7 (the renamed derivatives f_1, f_2, f_1_0, g_1, g_2, g_1_0, h_1; the extractor does not decode the EES names that carry the prime notation). Excluded variable: Obj (EES 8.37739e-05, CoolSolve 2.49901e-04) - the stored EES Objective is a stale record of an earlier iteration of the EES optimisation, since |g|+|f| of the stored f and g is 2.49901e-04. No other variable excluded. Max relative difference over the compared variables: 5.20e-04 (h, -0.884575 against -0.884116); f and g agree to 2.1e-08 and 3.2e-08. Shooting on the model (Newton on f(10) = g(10) = 0): f'(0) = 0.510213591117 and g'(0) = -0.615909650561, against White (2005) p. 162 (0.5102 and -0.6159): 2.7e-05 and 1.6e-05 relatively; the shipped slopes 0.510226344786 and -0.615925074583 agree to 5.2e-05 and 4.1e-05. The stored EES f'' and g'' satisfy the algebraic relations with -(g^2) to a relative difference of 0.0 and with +(g^2) to 2.6e-04, which shows that EES reads -g^2 as -(g^2) while CoolSolve reads it as (-g)^2 (CS-BUG-UNARY-POW).
